step_by_step_reasoning: The user provided an architecture diagram from AWS 'This is My Architecture' video featuring Love Bonito's e-commerce platform powered by Magento on Amazon EKS. End-user traffic flows through CloudFront CDN. Dynamic web requests pass to Varnish caching running on EC2, which forwards cache misses to Magento services on Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS). EKS pulls container images from Amazon ECR. Business data resides in Amazon Aurora MySQL with caching in ElastiCache Redis. Static media files are written/read by EKS via S3Fuse mounted onto an S3 bucket, which CloudFront serves globally to end users.

graph.name: Love Bonito E-commerce Architecture on AWS
graph.notes: Love Bonito transits its Magento e-commerce application onto AWS EKS with CloudFront, EC2 Varnish caching, Aurora MySQL, ElastiCache Redis, ECR, and S3Fuse file system integration.

nodes.name: USERS
nodes.notes: End-users accessing the Love Bonito omnichannel e-commerce platform.

nodes.name: CLOUDFRONT
nodes.notes: AWS CloudFront CDN delivering web content fast globally and forwarding dynamic requests to Varnish on EC2.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Amazon EC2 instance running Varnish cache to cache Magento content.

nodes.name: EKS
nodes.notes: Elastic Kubernetes Service hosting Magento applications split into web, admin, and cron workloads.

nodes.name: ECR
nodes.notes: Elastic Container Registry storing application Docker images pulled by EKS.

nodes.name: AURORA
nodes.notes: Amazon Aurora MySQL database holding business transactional data with multi-AZ replication.

nodes.name: ELASTICACHE
nodes.notes: ElastiCache Redis storing cached database queries to offload Aurora.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: S3 bucket storing media and assets, mounted into instances using S3Fuse.

edges.notes: Users direct all web traffic to CloudFront CDN.
CloudFront routes requests to Varnish running on EC2.
Varnish forwards cache misses on EC2 to Magento workloads running on EKS.
Magento applications on EKS query business data from Aurora MySQL.
EKS reads and writes database caches to ElastiCache Redis.
EKS mounts S3 bucket as a file system using S3Fuse to write asset content.
CloudFront directly serves static media assets stored in S3.
EKS pulls Docker container images from Elastic Container Registry.
